analysis:
Both changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/). EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift changes only the assertions in pagedPoolLocksStepWithSchedulerConfig (~lines 713-729) and adds widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry (~731-755). They now expect that Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS use a wide plain prefill chunk (EngineV2Factory.widePrefillChunkTokens) with soloPrefillStripeTokens == nil, while the paged pool's maxPrefillChunk stays at defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens. The same tests pin that SDK-chunk overrides still size the pool from max(chunk, stripe). Because the pool is sized from a fixed value rather than the wide chunk, the PagedSequenceKV precondition on windowed updates should not be exceeded. That invariant is asserted here but implemented in production code outside the supplied evidence, so I could not verify it. EngineV2PrefillGeometryTests.swift is a new test file (308 lines); only its first ~50 lines were visible, with no units of the body in text form. I saw tiny-model fixtures built from JSON configs and no network, credentials, or file I/O.

The tests introduce no production attack surface. They do not touch prefix-cache crypto, HMAC lookup tags, TTL or KEK handling (T-041), or the coordinator websocket, attestation, or App Attest boundaries. The existing SSD cache tests are unchanged, and the hermetic guard environment points the crash-loop guard at /dev/null. The production prefill-geometry change itself lives in files not supplied (EngineV2Factory). The next pass should confirm, in those files, that the wide chunk cannot overrun paged pool windows (an availability crash risk, T-010/T-029 class) and cannot raise per-step memory beyond the KV budget. That is a coverage limit, not a finding.
